children: The number of Australian job advertisements rose for a fourth straight month in August, private-sector data showed on Monday, suggesting labour demand remained healthy despite higher borrowing costs.

The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised interest rates three times to 4.35% this year and markets are fully pricing in another move by November as inflation has stayed stubbornly high. The labour market has remained resilient, with the unemployment rate at 4.5%.
• The number of job advertisements rose 2.5% in August from July, when they gained 1.9%, according to data from Australia and New Zealand Banking Group
and employment website Indeed. Ads were up 7.8% from a year earlier and remained 21.4% above their decade-long averages.

• The gain was in part driven by Christmas-related hiring, with a surge in retail and food service roles. Tech-related ads continued to ease, with demand in software development, data and analytics falling modestly.

• "We expect economic momentum to soften over the coming months as higher interest rates continue to restrain demand,"  said Jasmine Zheng, a senior economist at ANZ. "As a result, we anticipate Job Ads will gradually trend lower. However, given the resilience of the series, we expect the rise in the unemployment rate to be modest."
